title: Response to Singapore's Drop in 2025 World Talent Ranking
what_it_is: Response to Singapore's Drop in 2025 World Talent Ranking

sections.label: Perception factors in ranking change
sections.summary: Perception-based factors, including views on apprenticeships, training and brain drain, were a key driver of Singapore's 2025 ranking change.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: One key driver behind the change in Singapore's ranking in 2025 was in perception-based factors or indicators.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: In particular, how business executives viewed adequacy of apprenticeships, their perceptions of companies' prioritisation of employee training and their confidence in Singapore's ability to avoid brain drain.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: We will analyse these findings as well as other relevant data carefully, to better understand the underlying causes and see where and how we can do better.

sections.label: Education spending versus outcomes
sections.summary: Singapore ranked 63rd in public education expenditure as a share of GDP but second in PISA education outcomes.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: On the other hand, although we were ranked 63rd in terms of our public expenditure on education as a share of gross domestic product (GDP), we were second in the same survey on education outcomes, that is, the Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA) score.

sections.label: Confidence in global talent hub
sections.summary: Investing in people, business environment, connectivity and tech innovation is expected to keep Singapore a leading global talent hub.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: By investing in our people, enhancing our business environment, strengthening our connectivity and fostering a vibrant tech and innovation ecosystem, we are confident that Singapore will remain a leading global talent hub.

sections.label: Singapore's 2025 talent competitiveness rank
sections.summary: Singapore ranked seventh of 69 economies in 2025, down from second in 2024 but still top 10.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The first thing that I wanted to say was that it measures competitiveness across different countries and economies, and on this, although our ranking had dropped, we are actually still in the top 10.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, in other words, Singapore is still in this report, ranked the seventh most talent-competitive economy in 2025 out of 69 economies in 2025.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: And whilst this is a drop from second place in 2024, our general ranking has been on the uptrend over the last decade.

sections.label: Weaker investment and development factors
sections.summary: Weaker performance on investment and development in local talent came from perception factors, lower education expenditure and pupil-teacher ratio.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The first on investment and development in local talent, our weaker performance in the report on this factor was contributed by perception factors, decline in perception-based indicators on employee training and apprenticeships; and also, the second one was low public expenditure on education as a percentage of gross domestic product (GDP) – we went from 63rd to 65th and pupil-teacher ratio.

sections.label: Factors affecting this year's ranking
sections.summary: The ranking was affected by perceptions on employee training and apprenticeships, labour force growth and perceived availability of skilled labour.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In summary, the things which affected our ranking this year was perception on employee training and apprenticeships, labour force growth and the perception of the availability of skilled labour.
